speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; please describe how it started, its appearance, and if you have any fever or recent insect bites.

To help narrow down the cause, do you have any history of diabetes, immunosuppression, or recent travel to tropical areas?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis (suspected), potentially complicated by immunosuppression from Crohn's disease and prior corticosteroid use. The history of a mosquito/ant bite followed by a progressively enlarging, ulcerative lesion on an immunocompromised patient is highly suggestive of this parasitic infection. I recommend a skin biopsy for histopathology and PCR to confirm the diagnosis.
